newsitem.title: UK: U.S. data sparks big European stock gains.
newsitem.headline: U.S. data sparks big European stock gains.

text.p: European financial markets pushed sharply higher on Tuesday after crucial U.S. inflation and retail sales data smoothed fears of an early rise in interest rates.
U.S. treasury bonds popped higher on the data, making sure that Wall Street made a strong start as well.
European markets followed suit, with the London, Paris and Frankfurt stock markets striding further into record territory and government bonds reversing their earlier weakness.
Although the British and French bourses set new highs during the morning following Wall Street's record finish overnight, many European investors had been cautious ahead of the U.S. economic data.
The consumer prices (CPI) data for December showed inflation for all of 1996 rose at the fastest rate in six years, but core price rises for the month were subdued.
Christmas shopping boosted retail sales modestly during December, although the 0.6 percent rise was slightly higher than expected.
The figures showed that despite strong job growth and rising incomes, consumers have held spending in check. Economists said that might help curb inflation, reducing pressure on rates.

"We certainly got off to a fast start," said Alan Ackerman, chief market strategist at Fahnestock & Co after Wall Street raced ahead in the first few minutes of trading. "The CPI looks like a clear signal that things are on the right track and appears to have relaxed interest rate concerns."

On foreign exchange markets, the dollar soared briefly to 1.5955 marks after the data. The U.S. currency later came off its near 30-month high against the mark, but it nudged higher against the yen to around 116.80.
Comments by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan in Belgium earlier appeared to have little impact on markets.
Greenspan, who caused turmoil late last year by warning about irrational exuberance in financial markets, urged central banks not to take risks with inflation.
After the U.S. figures French stocks broke through the 2,400 point level for the first time, the CAC-40 index hitting a record 2,403.26 for a rise of nearly 1.7 percent.

"The bond market is very strong, the dollar is rising sharply, the U.S. figures were in line with expectations -- all is for the best in the best of all possible worlds," said EIFB analyst Pierre Vignaud.
In London, the FTSE 100 index powered on to a fresh trading high of 4,151.4, easily outpacing the 4,123.2 set on the last day of 1996.
The gains came despite fears of a rise in British interest rates at Wednesday's monetary policy meeting between the government and Bank of England.
"If we don't get one (a rate rise) this month we will probably get one in February," one dealer said.
Yet with investment funds still flush with cash, dealers said the FTSE could be pushed higher in coming sessions so long as other international markets keep on an upward trend.
German shares, which traded lower before the U.S. data, later rebounded with the IBIS DAX hitting a record 2,984.32 points in post-bourse electronic trading.
"Unless there are any upsets from the U.S., I think we can reach the 3,000 points this week now," one German trader said.
Lufthansa fell 84 pfennigs to 21.01 marks but was well off its lows after news that its shares were to be made non-freely transferable and worries about a possible capital increase.
CURRENCIES AT 1530 GMT
The dollar was trading at 116.73 yen and 1.5931 marks compared with 116.30 and 1.5890 late in Europe on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1530 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE 100 index was up 41.3 points, or 1.01 percent, at 4,148.6.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was up 36.15 points, or 1.53 percent, at 2,397.42.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed down 6.07 points, at 2,948.88. In later electronic trading, the IBIS DAX rose 19.24 points, or 0.65 percent, to 2,976.02.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $357.40, up 10 cents from the morning. Silver was unchanged at $4.72.
